objectives.text: Find the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle using a² + b² = c²
successCriteria: I can square both legs, add the squares and take the square root to find the hypotenuse
I can explain why the hypotenuse is not the sum of the two legs
assessmentPoints: Board answers during the squares-on-the-sides walkthrough
Hypotenuse answers in the closing worksheet activity

objectives.text: Find a short side when the hypotenuse and the other short side are known
successCriteria: I can rearrange a² + b² = c² to subtract the known square before taking the root
I can find the missing leg in a 5-12-13 style triangle
assessmentPoints: Pair answers in the hypotenuse-square activity
Closing worksheet answers on the missing-leg question

objectives.text: Use the converse of Pythagoras' theorem to test whether a triangle is right-angled
successCriteria: I can check whether the two smaller squares add to the largest square
I can state the conclusion the converse gives when the squares match or do not match
assessmentPoints: Responses when the trap is sprung
Closing worksheet answers on the converse question

objectives.text: Use TOA to write tan theta as opposite over adjacent
successCriteria: I can name the opposite and adjacent sides for a given angle
I can write tan theta = 3/4 for the 3-4-5 triangle and say why the flipped ratio is wrong
assessmentPoints: Partner explanations in the opening activity
Responses during the tangent discussion in the trap activity

activities.title: Meet the triangle and name the hypotenuse

differentiation.support: Provide the 3 by 3 and 4 by 4 grids pre-drawn so learners count the unit squares.

activities.title: Fill the square on the hypotenuse

differentiation.stretch: Ask pairs to test sides 5, 12 and 13 with the converse and justify the conclusion.
